name: Mars 2
summary: Soviet orbiter and lander sent in 1971. The orbiter reached Mars, but the descent module failed during entry.
highlights: Orbiter reached Mars and returned observations
Descent module failed during atmospheric entry
Impact site is an approximate coordinate

name: Mars 3
summary: Soviet orbiter and lander that made the first successful soft landing on Mars.
highlights: First soft landing on Mars
Lander transmitted for only about 20 seconds
Orbiter kept returning observations

name: Mars 6
summary: Soviet orbiter and lander launched in 1973. The lander sent data during descent, then went silent around landing.
highlights: Measured atmospheric conditions during descent
Contact lost around the time of landing
No surface operations were established

name: Viking 1
summary: NASA's first mission to land and operate on Mars. The lander studied soil and weather while the orbiter mapped the planet.
highlights: First successful NASA landing on Mars
Ran experiments searching for biological activity
Photographed the surface and tracked weather

name: Viking 2
summary: Second Viking mission. With Viking 1 it gave the first long-duration look at the Martian surface.
highlights: Returned images, weather and soil measurements
Ran biology experiments from the lander
Orbiter studied Mars from above

name: Mars Pathfinder / Sojourner
summary: Low-cost lander that delivered the Sojourner rover to Ares Vallis.
highlights: Sojourner examined rocks and soil up close
Airbag landing system demonstrated
Autonomous rover operations on another planet

name: Mars Express / Beagle 2
summary: ESA orbiter studying Mars since 2003. Its Beagle 2 lander reached the surface but never made contact.
highlights: One of the longest-running Mars orbiters
Studies surface, atmosphere, subsurface and water history
Beagle 2 landed but never established communications

name: Mars Exploration Rover Spirit
summary: NASA rover that searched Gusev Crater for evidence of past water and far outlasted its planned mission.
highlights: Explored Columbia Hills and Home Plate
Greatly exceeded its planned mission duration
Ended after becoming immobile and losing contact

name: Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity
summary: NASA rover that found extensive evidence that liquid water once shaped Meridiani Planum.
highlights: Operated for more than 14 years
Traveled more than 45 kilometers
Visited Endurance, Victoria and Endeavour craters

name: Phoenix
summary: NASA lander that dug into the northern plains and directly confirmed water ice beneath the surface.
highlights: Robotic arm dug into the soil
Analyzed soil chemistry and weather
Studied the polar environment

name: Mars Science Laboratory / Curiosity
summary: NASA rover investigating whether Gale Crater once offered conditions able to support microbial life.
highlights: Climbing the lower slopes of Mount Sharp
Found evidence of long-lived liquid water
Studies rocks, minerals and the atmosphere

name: InSight
summary: Stationary NASA lander built to study the deep interior of Mars rather than its surface.
highlights: Seismometer recorded marsquakes
Heat-flow experiment probed internal heat
Ended after dust reduced its power

name: Tianwen-1 / Zhurong
summary: China's first independent Mars mission: an orbiter plus the Zhurong rover, in a single mission.
highlights: Zhurong studied rocks, soil, weather and subsurface
Orbiter continues remote sensing and relay support
Orbited, landed and operated a rover in one mission

name: Mars 2020 / Perseverance
summary: NASA rover searching for signs of ancient microbial life and collecting rock samples for possible return to Earth.
highlights: Exploring an ancient river delta
Collects scientifically selected rock and soil samples
Carried Ingenuity, which flew on Mars
